# Resolve environment

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-docs.mjs. Edit the manifest, then run `make docs`. -->

Resolve KEY=SECRET_NAME mappings into masked environment variables

```yaml
- uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/actions/resolve-env@v1
```

## How it works

Turn `KEY=SECRET_NAME` mappings into masked environment variables for later steps.

The problem it solves: a reusable workflow can't know what a caller named its secrets.
threaditate needs `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`; another repo needs something else entirely.
Hardcoding names into a shared pipeline makes it not-shared.

So the caller passes a mapping — `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=SUPABASE_URL` — plus
`toJSON(secrets)`, and this action resolves each mapping against the secrets it was
handed and exports the result to `$GITHUB_ENV`.

Every resolved value is registered with `::add-mask::` before it is written, so it is
redacted in all subsequent log output. Values from `literal-vars` get the same treatment.

NOTE: `toJSON(secrets)` inside a reusable workflow only contains the secrets that
workflow declared, unless the caller used `secrets: inherit`. If a mapping resolves to
nothing, this action warns rather than failing — a missing optional analytics key
shouldn't take down the build — so check the log if a variable seems absent.

## Inputs

| Input | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mappings` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=SECRET_NAME` pairs resolved against `secrets-json`. |
| `literal-vars` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=value` pairs exported as-is (and masked). |
| `secrets-json` | no | `{}` | `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` from the calling workflow. |
| `mask-literals` | no | `true` | false to skip masking `literal-vars` (for genuinely public config). |
| `required` | no | `""` | Comma-separated KEY names that must resolve to a non-empty value. Missing ones fail the step instead of warning. |

## Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `resolved` | Comma-separated list of the variable names that were set. |
